name: get_warnings_attr
note: review: getWarningsAttr (Warn/Model.lean:268-279) now has the branches of :229-255, but PyErr_ExceptionMatches(PyExc_ImportError) (:234) is isA over excBase (Model.lean:227-243), a closed table that lacks ImportCycleError (the 3.15 ImportError subclass, Objects/exceptions.c:2025) and every non-builtin subclass, so GetWarningsAttrSpec part 2 ('any other import error propagates') is proven but false: measured on 3.15.2, a warnings module raising ImportCycleError or a user ImportError subclass on import is cleared and warn_explicit prints through show_warning; the callers (cShow, cDefault) also only ever pass a successful import and a present sys.modules entry.

name: warnings_lock
note: review: cAcquire (Filters.lean:241) is d+1 on a one-thread depth: _PyRecursiveMutex_Lock's owner tracking and blocking while another thread holds the lock cannot be expressed, and its one theorem (LockSpec part 1, release after acquire gives the depth back) holds for any counter.

name: warnings_unlock
note: review: cRelease (Filters.lean:245) fails only at depth 0, but _PyRecursiveMutex_TryUnlock fails whenever the caller is not the owner: measured on 3.15.2, _release_lock() raises 'cannot release un-acquired lock' while another thread holds the lock, so LockSpec's 'raises exactly when the lock is not held' is false outside the one-thread scope.
